subject: How to make sure xlim and ylim are the same without explicitly specifying them?

messages.author: c21e804e07c5e732
messages.subject: How to make sure xlim and ylim are the same without explicitly specifying them?
parts:
Hi,

I want to say a set of points after rotation are still similar to the
original ones. Therefore, I want the xlim and ylim be the same. But I
don't want to specify xlim and ylim explicity. I'm wondering if there
is an option so that qplot can figure out itself.

I also want the scaling be the same for both x and y axis. Currently,
I have to control the dimension of the output file. But I'd rather to
have something in the related to qplot function. Is there some option
that can control the x and y scaling?


set.seed(0)
m=10
X=data.frame(V1=rnorm(m), V2=rnorm(m))

prcomp_result=prcomp(X)

Y=do.call(
rbind
, lapply(
1:nrow(X)
, function(i) {
x=X[i,]
#browser()
data.frame(
V1=sum((x-prcomp_result$center)*prcomp_result$rotation[,1])
, V2=sum((x-prcomp_result$center)*prcomp_result$rotation[,2])
)
}
)
)

tmp=rbind(
data.frame(X, type='X')
, data.frame(Y, type='Y')
)

library(ggplot2)
p=qplot(V1, V2, data=tmp)+facet_grid(.~type)+xlim(-2,2)+ylim(-2,2)
ggsave(p, file=outfile, width=14, height=7)


--
Regards,
Peng
